rows: Severe thunderstorm winds blew down trees near Cuero.
Severe thunderstorm winds blew over trees and peeled back roofs of homes and businesses.
The DeWitt County sheriff's office reported nickel size hail.
A roof was blown off a camp house.
A large radio tower approximately 300 ft tall came down in 60 mph winds.
A NWS storm survey team determined the damage to a mobile home on VFW Road was caused by a tornado with estimated 70 to 80 mph winds.
Thunderstorm wind gusts, estimated at 45 knots, knocked down numerous tree limbs on Highway 111W.
Thunderstorm wind gusts, estimated at 35 to 45 mph, damaged a roof.
Thunderstorm wind gusts, estimated at 45 knots, pushed a travel trailer off its blocks. This storm also produced penny size hail.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts of approximately 50 kts which downed several trees and knocked down power lines in Cuero and blocked some rural roads.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 52 knots.
A thunderstorm produced nickel to quarter size hail for 15 minutes.

In downtown Yoakum, an apparent microburst caused wind damage to several homes on the southeast side of Yoakum near the intersection of Highways 77 and 111. Tree damage, shingles off roofs, and some metal buildings were heavily damaged.

A thunderstorm produced strong wind gusts estimated to be over 60 mph that blew over three recreational vehicles. One of the RVs was destroyed at the RV park on the north side of Yorktown. Other Areas of Yorktown sustained quite a bit of tree damage.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 58 mph that blew down trees in Cuero.
Large tree limbs were reported down by the public west of the city of Cuero.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph. The report from the Westoff Fire Department was relayed to the NWS by the DeWitt County emergency manager.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 80 mph that ripped the roof off a metal storage building and wrapped it around a tree in Westhoff.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that downed tree limbs and power lines along FM 766 just south of Rivercrest Ln. west of Hochheim.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that damaged the roof of a large barn near Thomaston.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that knocked down a large tree limb on Thomaston River Rd.
A thunderstorm produced a wind gust measured at 65 mph by a spotter in Nordheim.
Thunderstorms produced wind gusts estimated at 65 mph that blew down several trees and caused minor roof damage in Yorktown.
A large tree was uprooted and numerous other trees were damaged at a residence when strong thunderstorm winds blew across the area.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 75 mph that uprooted a 30 foot tree northeast of Hochheim.
A thunderstorm produced ping pong ball size hail along Hwy 72 between Yorktown and Cuero.
A thunderstorm produced half dollar size hail southwest of Cuero.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail southeast of Cuero.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail north of Cuero.
A thunderstorm produced hail up to the size of golf balls in Yoakum.
A thunderstorm produced golf ball size hail in Cuero.
A thunderstorm produced ping pong ball size hail near the intersection of E. Clayton St. and N. Clinton St. in Cuero.
A thunderstorm produced golf ball size hail at the intersection of Tulley Rd. and Bubba Palmer Rd. in Cuero.
A thunderstorm produced hail up to golf ball size in Meyersville. Most of the hail was less than quarter size.
